candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether Fort Worth magnet output is qualified for defense-relevant customers using compliant non-Chinese feedstock, not merely producing nominal magnet capacity.
candidates.next_evidence: Track customer qualification disclosures, DoD offtake terms, NdPr/heavy-REE source tracing, magnet shipment volumes, and whether defense primes cite MP as an approved source.
candidates.node_relation: Reference anchor for U.S. vertically integrated rare-earth magnet supply: Mountain Pass feedstock, NdPr separation, metal/alloy conversion, and Fort Worth NdFeB magnet manufacturing.

candidates.theme_relation: Direct beneficiary of defense industrial policy, DFARS/NDAA sourcing pressure, DoD funding, price-floor support, and government-backed magnet offtake.
candidates.why_include: MP is the clearest U.S.-listed benchmark for the node because official company and DoD materials show rare-earth mining/separation, heavy rare-earth separation support, and U.S. NdFeB magnet manufacturing buildout.
candidates.why_underfollowed: Not underfollowed; included only as the reference lane so smaller candidates can be compared against a known integrated standard.

candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether produced magnets are qualified by defense or dual-use OEMs using documented non-Chinese feedstock and whether Brazil/European-linked feedstock is treated as compliant under relevant defense rules.
candidates.next_evidence: Verify production ramp at Stillwater, Blacksburg permitting/capex timeline, customer qualification announcements, feedstock chain-of-custody, and any DoD/prime contractor qualification milestones.
candidates.node_relation: Emerging U.S.-listed mine-to-magnet candidate with Stillwater magnet production, planned South Carolina magnet/metals capacity, and federal support for NdFeB magnet and alloy production.
candidates.sector_or_industry: Rare earth mining, processing, metals, alloys, and NdFeB permanent magnets
candidates.theme_relation: Potential second anchor for U.S./allied compliant magnet capacity if its domestic and allied feedstock, metallization, strip-casting, and customer qualification plans execute.
candidates.why_include: Official NIST and state/company releases indicate USA Rare Earth is building mine-to-magnet capacity, including NdFeB magnet and rare-earth metal/alloy production. This maps closely to the bottleneck hypothesis.
candidates.why_underfollowed: It is newer to public markets than MP, has a more complex asset map across Oklahoma, South Carolina, Texas, Colorado, Europe, and Brazil, and may be screened as a mining/SPAC story rather than as a qualification bottleneck candidate.

candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether its NdPr, Dy, Tb, or other oxides pass magnet-maker and OEM qualification at commercial scale, with traceable non-Chinese monazite/feedstock.

candidates.theme_relation: Second-order beneficiary of policy pressure if magnet bottlenecks shift from mines to qualified separated oxides, especially dysprosium/terbium inputs needed for high-performance defense and high-temperature magnets.
candidates.why_include: Energy Fuels is not a magnet producer, but official releases show rare-earth oxide production, a Vulcan Elements MOU for an ex-China magnet supply chain, and heavy rare-earth oxide pilot milestones. That makes it a potential feedstock qualification chokepoint.
candidates.why_underfollowed: It is often labeled primarily as a uranium company, so screens may miss rare-earth oxide qualification exposure and the role of heavy rare earths in NdFeB magnet performance.

candidates.theme_relation: Policy optionality candidate if defense procurement and supply-chain illumination favor U.S.-based critical mineral deposits that can support downstream magnet qualification partners.
candidates.why_include: NioCorp’s Elk Creek materials describe a domestic critical minerals project with rare-earth oxide resources and technical/economic analysis for adding magnetic rare-earth oxides. This gives it optionality, but the evidence is much weaker than producers or funded magnet makers.
candidates.why_underfollowed: It is usually viewed as a niobium/scandium/titanium development project, so rare-earth magnet feedstock optionality can be hidden inside a broader, pre-production critical minerals story.

evidence.claim: Defense and dual-use supply chains remain shallow beyond tier-one firms, with DoD and primes often lacking visibility beyond lower tiers; this supports searching for subtier chokepoints rather than only prime contractors or headline mines.

Recent critical-minerals policy discussion is shifting from simple sourcing restrictions toward supply-chain transition requirements, making supplier qualification and compliant availability central questions.
evidence.source_title: Defense Critical Minerals Policy is Moving From Sourcing Restrictions to Supply Chain Requirements - The Fuse

evidence.claim: MP Materials states that its Fort Worth Independence facility transforms refined rare-earth materials from Mountain Pass into metals, alloys, and finished NdFeB magnets.
The U.S. Department of Defense awarded MP Materials $35 million to build U.S. heavy rare-earth separation capacity as part of rare-earth supply-chain resiliency efforts.
evidence.source_title: DoD Awards $35 Million to MP Materials to Build U.S. Heavy Rare Earth Separation Capacity

evidence.claim: NIST announced a finalized CHIPS Program agreement with USA Rare Earth for up to $1.6 billion to support a mine-to-magnet strategy, including production capability for rare-earth metal alloy and NdFeB magnets.
evidence.source_title: The Department of Commerce’s CHIPS Program Finalizes Definitive Agreement With USA Rare Earth For Up To $1.6 Billion To Support The Company’s “Mine-to-Magnet” Strategy

evidence.claim: South Carolina announced USA Rare Earth selected Cherokee County for a facility to produce NdFeB permanent magnets and refined rare-earth metals.
evidence.source_title: USA Rare Earth, Inc. selects Cherokee County for first South Carolina operation

evidence.claim: Energy Fuels and Vulcan Elements signed an MOU to collaborate on a domestic rare-earth magnet supply chain independent of China.
evidence.source_title: Energy Fuels and Vulcan Elements Join Forces to Advance U.S. Rare Earth Magnet Security

evidence.claim: Energy Fuels announced first U.S. primary production of a critical heavy rare-earth material in decades and highlighted the need for magnet manufacturer and OEM validation.
evidence.source_title: Energy Fuels Announces First U.S. Primary Production of Critical Heavy Rare Earth Material in Decades

evidence.claim: NioCorp says it is conducting technical and economic analyses on adding magnetic rare-earth oxides to its planned Elk Creek product suite, and describes NdPr oxide as indispensable to high-performance rare-earth permanent magnets.
evidence.source_title: Elk Creek Project | NioCorp Developments Ltd.

evidence.claim: NioCorp’s 2022 feasibility-study filing described Elk Creek as containing an estimated 632.9 kilotonnes of contained total rare-earth oxides in the indicated mineral resource category.
evidence.source_title: NioCorp Files NI 43-101 Technical Report on its 2022 Elk Creek Critical Minerals Project Feasibility Study

memory_update.text: MP is the reference anchor for U.S. integrated rare-earth magnet capacity; do not let it crowd out smaller qualification/feedstock candidates in later layers.
USAR is a priority underfollowed candidate for Layer 2 because federal support and planned NdFeB/metals capacity map directly to the non-Chinese-feedstock magnet qualification node.
UUUU should be tracked as an oxide/feedstock qualification gate rather than a magnet manufacturer; key survival test is magnet-maker/OEM validation of NdPr and heavy REE oxides at scale.

NB is a speculative shadow candidate: domestic magnetic rare-earth oxide optionality exists, but it should not survive later layers without financing, feasibility, offtake, and downstream qualification evidence.

Need a later pass on private or non-U.S.-listed magnet makers such as Vulcan Elements, Noveon, e-VAC/Vacuumschmelze, Ucore, Neo Performance, and Lynas as customer/supplier anchors even if they are not U.S.-listed common-stock candidates.

summary: Expanded the universe around the chokepoint that defense-relevant rare-earth magnet capacity may be constrained less by nominal ex-China magnet tonnage and more by qualified oxide-to-metal-to-alloy-to-NdFeB magnet chains using compliant non-Chinese feedstock. The reference lane is MP Materials because it is the clearest U.S. integrated mine-to-magnet anchor with DoD support. The underfollowed lane highlights USA Rare Earth, Energy Fuels, and NioCorp as smaller or less obvious public assets tied to magnet manufacturing, separated NdPr/heavy rare-earth oxide qualification, or future domestic feedstock optionality. These are research candidates only, not buy/sell recommendations.
